novelty_flags.label: thm:tid-dichotomy / oeq:uniform-normal-form literature survey
novelty_flags.one_line: The survey omits Ferreira--Assaad (AAAI 2024), a published complete SCG identifiability result for direct effects under linearity and no hidden confounding; it does not subsume this total-effect kernel, but is the closest missing completeness comparator and must be explicitly separated.

source_verification_receipts.version: TMLR, May 2025; primary PDF access redirected by publisher, with arXiv v2 corroboration
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work is published in TMLR and presents sufficient graphical conditions for identifying SCG micro total effects with latent confounding.
The paper gives a bound depending on width and maximum lag for applying ID to a fully specified causal time-series graph.
The paper distinguishes micro from macro queries and proves do-calculus sound and complete for macro total effects in SCGs.
The fixed-ADMG ID algorithm returns an observational expression or FAIL with a hedge witnessing nonidentification.
The paper gives a sound-and-complete conditional-effect identification algorithm for a PAG representing a finite Markov-equivalence class.
The paper gives necessary-and-sufficient conditions and a pseudo-linear decision algorithm for the adjustment criterion in time-series SCGs.
The paper develops weight-based and influence-function estimation strategies for identifiable effects in fixed hidden-variable DAGs.
The paper develops nested Markov properties for ADMGs, including the fixed-graph fixing/intrinsic-set framework used as background here.
The paper gives a complete SCG identifiability characterization and finite adjustment sets for linear direct effects under no hidden confounding.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Ferreira--Assaad (AAAI 2024) to the bibliography and explicitly prove a separation table: its linear, causally sufficient direct-effect setting versus this nonparametric latent-confounded micro-total-effect target.

Add a second formal comparator boundary against Yvernes--Devijver--Gaussier (2025), with a concrete SCG where complete common adjustment fails or is inapplicable but the proposed fixing route succeeds.

Specify the finite encoding of a transducer state and give a worked small-input TID-SCG trace, including its output cylinder functional or lag-switch certificate, so the algorithmic-identifiability claim has an auditable computational object.

recommended_next_step: Revise the survey and comparator boundary around published complete SCG identification results, then continue this angle to Stage 0.
